Function to prep data for ssf

prep.data.ssf <- function(tracks, cov, fit.col.name = NULL, id.col.name = "id", 
                          x.name = "X_UTM", y.name = "Y_UTM", t.name = "DatetimeLocal",
                          mask = NULL, dt = 15, n.random.extra = 50, n.avail = 30){
  
  
  # Create observed steps
  tracks.id <- tracks %>% nest(.by= c(!! sym(id.col.name), !!! syms(fit.col.name)))
  steps.id <- tracks.id %>% 
    mutate(trk = map(data, function(d) {
      d %>% make_track(.x = !! sym(x.name), .y = !! sym(y.name), .t= !! sym(t.name)) %>%
        track_resample(rate = minutes(dt), tolerance = minutes(1)) %>% steps_by_burst()})) 
  
  
  steps.avail <- steps.id
  steps.avail$rp <- NULL
  
  # We want the parameters used to create the control steps to be from the same distribution
  # We do not want the parameters to be taken for each individual separately
  data <- steps.avail %>% 
    dplyr::select(!! sym(id.col.name), !!! syms(fit.col.name), trk) %>%  
    unnest(cols= c(trk)) 
  gamma_par <-  data$sl_ %>% fit_distr("gamma")
  vonmises_par <- data$ta_ %>% fit_distr("vonmises")
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(steps.avail)){
    steps.avail[[i,"rp"]][[1]] <- steps.id[[i,"trk"]][[1]] %>% 
      random_steps(n_control = n.random.extra, 
                   sl_distr = make_gamma_distr(shape = gamma_par$params$shape,
                                               scale = gamma_par$params$scale,
                                               vcov = gamma_par$vcov),
                   ta_distr = make_vonmises_distr(kappa = vonmises_par$params$kappa,
                                                  vcov = vonmises_par$vcov))
  }
  
  
  for(i in seq_along(cov)){
    steps.avail <- steps.avail %>% 
      mutate(rp = map(rp, function(d){
      extract_covariates(d,cov[[i]])}))
  }
  
  steps.avail <- steps.avail %>% 
    dplyr::select(!! sym(id.col.name), !!! syms(fit.col.name), rp) %>%  
    unnest(cols= c(rp))  
  
  # Important: the `step_id_` will have erroneously similar names across individuals. We change the name here.
  steps.avail$step_id_ <- paste(steps.avail[[id.col.name]], steps.avail$step_id_, sep="_")
  steps.avail.sf <- st_as_sf(filter(steps.avail, !is.na(ta_)), coords = c("x2_", "y2_"), remove=FALSE)
  st_crs(steps.avail.sf) <- chosen.proj
  
  
  # Remove the control points that are in habitat that are masked (e.g., land for narwhals)
  for(i in seq_along(mask)){
    steps.avail.sf$mask <- rowSums(st_intersects(steps.avail.sf, mask[[i]], sparse=FALSE))
    steps.avail.sf <- subset(steps.avail.sf, !mask)
  }
    
   
  steps.avail.11 <- as.data.frame(steps.avail.sf) %>%
      group_by(step_id_) %>% filter(row_number() >= 1 & row_number() <= n.avail + 1)
  
  # Get the log sl and cos ta. And numeric case for poisson distribution
  steps.avail.11$ln_sl <- log(steps.avail.11$sl_)
  steps.avail.11$cos_ta <- cos(steps.avail.11$ta_)
  steps.avail.11$case_num <- as.numeric(steps.avail.11$case_)
  
  return(list(steps.id = steps.id, steps.avail = steps.avail.11, 
              gamma_par=gamma_par, vonmises_par=vonmises_par))
}

Let’s calculate distance from shore. Distance from shore for habitat selection should be at the end of the step (select where to go), but for the movement kernel it should be at beginning of the step (movement characteristics based on where they are).

This will take a few minutes to run.

narwhals.avail.sf <- st_as_sf(narwhals.steps.avail$steps.avail, 
                              coords = c("x2_", "y2_"), remove = FALSE, 
                              crs = chosen.proj)
narwhals.avail.sf.start <- st_as_sf(narwhals.steps.avail$steps.avail, 
                                    coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), remove = FALSE, 
                                    crs = chosen.proj)

land.1 <- st_cast(st_union(land),  to = 'MULTILINESTRING') # Need to make it a line to 
narwhals.avail.sf$distShore.end <- 
  as.numeric(st_distance(narwhals.avail.sf, land.1))/1000
narwhals.avail.sf$distShore.start <- 
  as.numeric(st_distance(narwhals.avail.sf.start, land.1))/1000

Format data and binary variable as 0 and 1.

all.steps <- as.data.frame(narwhals.avail.sf)
all.steps$Healed.Scars <- as.numeric(all.steps$Healed.Scars)

Fit models

Function to fit a SSF.

fit.poisson.rs <- function(formula, data, 
                           start = list(theta = c(log(1e6), 0)), 
                           map = list(theta = factor(c(NA, 1)))){
  ssf <- glmmTMB(formula, family = poisson, 
                 data = data, start = start, map = map)
  return(ssf)
}

AICc table function

AICcTable <- function(m, ...){
  namesObj <- names(tibble::lst(m, ...))
  namesObj[1] <- deparse(substitute(m))
  AICc.table <- AICc(m, ...)
  row.names(AICc.table) <- namesObj
  AICc.table <- AICc.table %>% 
    mutate(deltaAICc = AICc - min(AICc, na.rm = TRUE))
  AICc.table[order(AICc.table$deltaAICc), ]
}

We will look at four SSFs that compare the environmental covariates at locations associated with the observed animal movement at time \(t\) (encoded as \(y_{n,t,j} = 1\) for \(j = 0\)) to control locations (encoded as \(y_{n,t,j} = 0\) for \(j = 1, ..., J\)). Here, these SSFs model the locations of \(n = 1, ..., 14\) narwhals for \(j = 0, 1,..., 50\) used and control locations. The environmental covariate of interest is distance to shore, and we assumed that distance to shore at the end of step \(j\) \(d_{n,t,j}\) affects the selection function, while distance to shore at the start of a step \(j\) \(d_{n,t-1,j}\) affects the movement kernel. We use the mixed Poisson model framework outlined in Muff et al. (2020).

Model 1 (baseline model): Scars ignored

The SSF models the step of individual \(n\) at time \(t\), \(y_{n,t,j}\), which take the value of 1 for used step (\(j = 0\)) and 0 for control points (\(j = 1, ..., J\)), as:

\[\mu_{n,t,j} = \exp(\beta_{0,n,t} + \beta_{1,n} d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{l} l_{n,t,j} + \beta_{2} d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{\ln} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_3 d_{n,t-1,j} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_4 d_{n,t-1,j}^2 \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \\ \beta_{\theta} \cos(\theta_{n,t,j})), \qquad y_{n,t,j} \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{n,t,j}),\]

where for the \(n^{th}\) individual at time \(t\) for step \(j\), \(d_{n,t,j}\) represents the distance to shore, \(l_{n,t,j}\) the step length, and \(\theta_{n,t,j}\) the turning angle. The coefficient \(\beta_{0,n,t}\) is the step-specific intercept of animal \(n\) at time \(t\), which is modelled as a random effect \(\beta_{0,n,t} \sim \text{N}(0,1000000^2)\), while the coefficients \(\beta_{1,n}\) is the coefficient associated with the habitat selection function and is modelled with a random effect for which we estimate the mean and standard deviation: \(\beta_{1,n} \sim \text{N}(\beta_1, \sigma_1^2)\). The rest of the terms are associated with the movement kernel, where \(\beta_2\), \(\beta_{l}\), \(\beta_{\ln}\), \(\beta_{\theta}\), \(\beta_{3}\), and \(\beta_4\) are coefficients associated with the step lengths and turning angles. As explained in Avgar et al. (2015), the inclusion of the step length and its natural logarithm is a way to model the step length distribution as a Gamma distribution. Similarly, the inclusion of the cosine of the turning angle is a method to model the turning angle distribution as a Von Mises distribution. Here, \(\beta_2\), \(\beta_3\), and \(\beta_4\) allow for the movement kernel, specifically the step length distribution, to vary as a function of distance to shore.

ssf.noscars <- fit.poisson.rs(formula = case_num ~ -1 + 
                                # Habitat selection function
                                distShore.end +
                                # Movement kernel
                                sl_ + distShore.start:sl_ + 
                                ln_sl + distShore.start:ln_sl + 
                                I(distShore.start^2):ln_sl +
                                cos_ta + 
                                (1 | step_id_) +
                                (0 + distShore.end | ID), 
                              data = all.steps)

No converge problem messages.

The three other models use healed scars as a health proxy by including interactions in the model with the variable \(s_n\), which takes the value of 1 when healed scars are present on the individual \(n\) and 0 when individual \(n\) has no healed scars.

Model 2: Scar information in the selection function

As a base, we are using model 1 described above. However, to allow for the selection function to differ between individuals with and without scars, we include an interaction between presence of scars \(s_n\) and distance to shore at the end of the step, \(d_{n,t,j}\):

\[\mu_{n,t,j} = \exp(\beta_{0,n,t} + \beta_{1,n} d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_5 s_n d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{l} l_{n,t,j} + \beta_{2} d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{\ln} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_3 d_{n,t-1,j} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_4 d_{n,t-1,j}^2 \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \\ \beta_{\theta} \cos(\theta_{n,t,j})), \qquad y_{n,t,j} \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{n,t,j}),\]

where \(\beta_5\) represents the coefficient quantifying the relationship between the presence of scars and distance to shore.

ssf.sel.healed <- fit.poisson.rs(formula = case_num ~ -1 + 
                                   # Habitat selection
                                   distShore.end + 
                                   distShore.end:Healed.Scars +
                                   # Movement kernel
                                   sl_ + distShore.start:sl_ + 
                                   ln_sl  + distShore.start:ln_sl  +
                                   I(distShore.start^2):ln_sl  + 
                                   cos_ta + 
                                   (1 | step_id_) +
                                   (0 + distShore.end | ID), 
                                  data = all.steps)

Model 3: Scar information in the movement kernel

As a base, we are using model 1 described above. However, to allow for the relationship with speed and distance to shore to differ between individuals with and without scars, we include an interaction between the presence of scars \(s_n\), step length \(l_{n,t,j}\), and distance to shore at the start of the step \(d_{n,t-1,j}\):

\[\mu_{n,t,j} = \exp(\beta_{0,n,t} + \beta_{1,n} d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{l} l_{n,t,j} + \beta_{2} d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_6 s_n d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{\ln} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_3 d_{n,t-1,j} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_4 d_{n,t-1,j}^2 \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \\ \beta_{\theta} \cos(\theta_{n,t,j})), \qquad y_{n,t,j} \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{n,t,j}),\]

where \(\beta_6\) quantifies the relationship between the scars, step length, and distance to shore.

ssf.mov.healed <- fit.poisson.rs(formula = case_num ~ -1 + 
                                   # Habitat selection
                                   distShore.end + 
                                   # Movement kernel
                                   sl_ + distShore.start:sl_ + 
                                   distShore.start:Healed.Scars:sl_ + 
                                   ln_sl + distShore.start:ln_sl + I(distShore.start^2):ln_sl + 
                                   cos_ta + 
                                   (1|step_id_) +
                                   (0 + distShore.end | ID), 
                                  data = all.steps)

Model 4: Scar information in both the selection function and the movement kernel

To allow the presence of scars to affect both the selection function and the movement kernel, we simply combine models 2 and 3:

\[\mu_{n,t,j} = \exp(\beta_{0,n,t} + \beta_{1,n} d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_5 s_n d_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{l} l_{n,t,j} + \beta_{2} d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_6 s_n d_{n,t-1,j} l_{n,t,j} + \\ \beta_{\ln} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_3 d_{n,t-1,j} \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \beta_4 d_{n,t-1,j}^2 \ln(l_{n,t,j}) + \\ \beta_{\theta} \cos(\theta_{n,t,j})), \qquad y_{n,t,j} \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{n,t,j}).\]

ssf.mov.sel.healed <- fit.poisson.rs(formula = case_num ~ -1 + 
                                       # Habitat selection
                                       distShore.end + distShore.end:Healed.Scars +
                                       # Movement kernel
                                       sl_ + distShore.start:sl_ + 
                                       distShore.start:Healed.Scars:sl_ + 
                                       ln_sl  + distShore.start:ln_sl  +
                                       I(distShore.start^2):ln_sl  + 
                                       cos_ta + 
                                       (1|step_id_) +
                                       (0 + distShore.end | ID),
                                     data = all.steps)

Interpreting the results

Parameters for the gamma distribution used to sample the control points.

b1_shape <- narwhals.steps.avail$gamma_par$params$shape
b2_scale <- narwhals.steps.avail$gamma_par$params$scale
b3_kappa <- narwhals.steps.avail$vonmises_par$params$kappa

Functions to calculate the estimated parameters of the gamma.

shape.ssf <- function(b1_shape, model, dist){
  gamma.shape.ssf <- b1_shape + 
    summary(model)$coef$cond["ln_sl",1] +
    dist*summary(model)$coef$cond["distShore.start:ln_sl",1]  + 
    (dist^2)*summary(model)$coef$cond["ln_sl:I(distShore.start^2)",1] 
  return(gamma.shape.ssf)
}

scale.ssf <- function(b2_scale, model, dist, healed = FALSE){
  sl.healed.dist <- which(str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "sl_") & 
             str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "Healed.Scars") & 
             str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "distShore.start"))
  sl.dist <- which(str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "sl_") & 
             !str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "Healed.Scars") & 
             str_detect(row.names(summary(model)$coef$cond), "distShore.start"))
  gamma.scale.ssf <- 1/((b2_scale^(-1)) - 
                          summary(model)$coef$cond["sl_",1] -
                          dist*summary(model)$coef$cond[sl.dist, 1] -
                          dist*ifelse(healed, 
                                      summary(model)$coef$cond[sl.healed.dist,1],
                                      0))
  return(gamma.scale.ssf)
}


# Simple for the angle distribution, since no other covariate has an effect on the angle
kappa.ssf <- function(b3_kappa, model){
  vmises.kappa.ssf <- b3_kappa + summary(model)$coef$cond["cos_ta",1]
  return(vmises.kappa.ssf)
}


# Function for mean step length
sl.ssf <- function(b1_shape, b2_scale, model, dist, healed = FALSE){
  gamma.shape.ssf <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, model, dist)
  gamma.scale.ssf <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, model, dist, healed)
  mean.sl <- gamma.shape.ssf*gamma.scale.ssf
  sd.sl <- sqrt(gamma.shape.ssf*(gamma.scale.ssf^2))
  return(cbind(mean.sl, sd.sl))
}

bb <- 1

mean.obs.sl.healed.T <- aggregate(sl_ ~ new_bin_mid,

Mean step length plots.

out.size <- 0.1

mov.plot <- function(names, healed){
  if(!healed){
    m.plot <- ggplot() + 
      geom_boxplot(data = subset(all.steps, case_num ==1), 
                   aes(x = new_bin_mid, y=sl_/1000, 
                       group = as.factor(new_bin_mid)), 
                   fill = alpha(col.all,0.5),
                   outlier.size = out.size,
                   linewidth = 0.2) +
      geom_point(data = mean.obs.sl.all, 
                 aes(x = new_bin_mid, y = sl_/1000), 
                 col = col.all, pch=17, size = 0.5) +
      geom_line(data= models.pred, 
                aes(x=dist.seq, y = !! sym(paste(names, "mean", sep="."))))
  }else{
    m.plot <- ggplot() + 
      geom_boxplot(data = subset(all.steps, 
                                 case_num == 1 & Healed.Scars == TRUE), 
                   aes(x = new_bin_mid, y = sl_/1000, 
                       group = as.factor(new_bin_mid)), 
                   fill = alpha(pred.col["TRUE"], 0.5), 
                   outlier.colour = pred.col["TRUE"], 
                   outlier.size = out.size,
                   position = position_nudge(x = -nudge.v), 
                   width = 0.25,
                   linewidth = 0.2) +
      geom_point(data = mean.obs.sl.healed.T, 
                 aes(x = new_bin_mid-nudge.v, y = sl_/1000), 
                 col = pred.col["TRUE"], pch = 17, size = 0.5) +
      geom_line(data = models.pred, 
                aes(x = dist.seq, y = !! sym(paste(names, "T.mean", sep="."))),
                col = pred.col["TRUE"]) +
      geom_boxplot(data = subset(all.steps, 
                                 case_num == 1 & Healed.Scars == FALSE), 
               aes(x = new_bin_mid, y = sl_/1000, 
                   group = as.factor(new_bin_mid)), 
               fill = alpha(pred.col["FALSE"],0.5), 
               outlier.size = out.size,
               outlier.colour = pred.col["FALSE"],
               position = position_nudge(x = +nudge.v), 
               width = 0.25,
               linewidth = 0.2) +
      geom_point(data = mean.obs.sl.healed.F, 
                 aes(x = new_bin_mid+nudge.v, y = sl_/1000), 
                 col = pred.col["FALSE"], pch = 17, size = 0.5) +
      geom_line(data = models.pred, 
                aes(x = dist.seq, y = !! sym(paste(names, "F.mean", sep="."))),
                col = pred.col["FALSE"])
  }
  
  m.plot <- m.plot + xlab("Distance to shore (km)") + ylab("Step length (km)") + 
    guides(Healed.T = guide_custom(grid::circleGrob(r = unit(0.1, "cm"),
                                                  gp = grid::gpar(fill = pred.col["TRUE"],
                                                                  col = NA)), 
                                 title = "With healed scars", order = 3, 
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = 
                                                 element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top")),
           Healed.F = guide_custom(grid::circleGrob(r = unit(0.1, "cm"),
                                                  gp = grid::gpar(fill = pred.col["FALSE"],
                                                                  col = NA)), 
                                 title = "Without scars", order = 2, 
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = 
                                                 element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top")),
           No.scars = guide_custom(grid::circleGrob(r = unit(0.1, "cm"), 
                                                  gp = grid::gpar(fill = "black", 
                                                                  col = NA)), 
                                 title = "Ignoring scars", order = 1, 
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = 
                                                 element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top"))) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    theme_classic() + 
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.7)),
          axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.1),
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.1))
    
  return(m.plot)
}

Map predictions

First create a distance to shore raster.

rast.grid <- rast(extent = ext(narwhals.avail.sf), 
                  nrows=150, ncols=150, crs = crs(land))
landR <- as.numeric(rasterize(land, rast.grid))
landR[is.na(landR)] <- 0

shore <- distance(landR, vect(land.1))/1000
names(shore) <- "distShore"

shore.w <- shore
shore.w[landR == 1] <- NA

Prediction map of SSF using the naive method (sensu Signer et al. 2017). Habitat selection coefficient * covariate. Below we will look at the utilization distribution (UD).

ssf.map.noscars <- exp(summary(ssf.noscars)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w)
ssf.map.sel.healed.F <- 
  exp((summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w))
ssf.map.sel.healed.T <- 
  exp((summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w) +
        (summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end:Healed.Scars",1] * shore.w))
ssf.map.mov.healed <- 
  exp(summary(ssf.mov.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w)
ssf.map.mov.sel.healed.F <- 
  exp((summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w))
ssf.map.mov.sel.healed.T <- 
  exp((summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore.w) +
        (summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end:Healed.Scars",1] * shore.w))


ssf.maps <- rast(list(noscars = ssf.map.noscars, 
                      sel.healed.F = ssf.map.sel.healed.F,
                      sel.healed.T = ssf.map.sel.healed.T,
                      mov.healed = ssf.map.mov.healed, 
                      mov.sel.healed.F = ssf.map.mov.sel.healed.F,
                      mov.sel.healed.T = ssf.map.mov.sel.healed.T))

Function to plot each plot separately.

land.col <- "floralwhite"
ssf.min.col <- "#ffffcc"
ssf.mid.col <- "#41b6c4"
ssf.max.col <- "#0c2c84"

# For common colour bar
val.range <- range(as.data.frame(ssf.maps))

# Function for maps
mapping <- function(model.name, col.box){
  map <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = ssf.maps[[model.name]]) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low=ssf.min.col, mid=ssf.mid.col, high=ssf.max.col,
                      midpoint = mean(val.range), limit = val.range, na.value = NA) +
    geom_sf(data=land, fill=land.col) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(st_bbox(ssf.maps[[model.name]])[1], st_bbox(ssf.maps[[model.name]])[3]),
           ylim = c(st_bbox(ssf.maps[[model.name]])[2], st_bbox(ssf.maps[[model.name]])[4]), expand = FALSE) +
    theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = col.box, fill=NA, linewidth = 0.5),
          legend.title = element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
          legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          legend.position = "top",
          axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(70, 80, by =1)) + 
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-90, -80, by = 5)) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title = "SSF", order = 4,
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top"))) +
    theme(plot.margin = unit(plot.mar.l, 'lines'))
  return(map)
}

Utilization Distribution

We can also look at the UD obtained from the step selection analysis. To estimate the UD, we used eq (10) in Potts and Börger (2022) and followed the procedure defined in Appendix E of their paper. Specifically, we use the exact method to derive the UD from the movement kernel, involving eigenvalues and eigenvectors. We note that using a simulation based approach is difficult for this case study, because the narwhals inhabit narrow and intricate fjords. Thus the simulation need to run a long time to explore the full area. While we already have the selection function for each model, we also need the corresponding movement distribution function to get the movement kernel. Since narwhals are marine mammals, we will only consider locations in the raster that correspond to water cells.

# Selects location that are on water
water_cells <- which(values(landR) == 0) 
# Extract their corresponding coordinates in the raster
coords_proj <- xyFromCell(rast.grid, water_cells) 
# Number of locations to evaluate to get the movement kernel that will be a n x n matrix
# row is start point and column is end point of the movement
n <- nrow(coords_proj) 

# Derive distance to shore covariate
# Covariate that is used in all models: distance to shore
shore_vals <- values(shore.w)[water_cells]  
# Each column has the same value: corresponding to the distance to shore at the end point
shore_vals_end <- matrix(shore_vals, nrow = n, ncol = n, byrow = TRUE) 
# Each row as same value: corresponding to the distance to shore at the start point. 
shore_vals_start <- matrix(shore_vals, nrow = n, ncol = n) 

# Derive the matrix of step length: 
# row i and col j corresponds to step length from ith location (start) -> jth location (end)
sf_points <- st_as_sf(as.data.frame(coords_proj), 
                      coords = c("x", "y"), crs = chosen.proj)
step_length_matrix <- st_distance(sf_points, sf_points)/1000
step_length_matrix <- matrix(as.numeric(step_length_matrix), 
                             nrow = nrow(step_length_matrix))

The movement depends on the individuals’ starting locations, so we use shore_vals_start as the matrix of covariates for the movement parameters. For each model, we now derive the associated movement parameters.

# For Model 1: ssf.map.noscars
shape1 <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.noscars,
                    shore_vals_start)
scale1 <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.noscars,
                    shore_vals_start, healed=FALSE) 


# For Model 2: ssf.map.sel.healed.F and ssf.map.sel.healed.T
shape2 <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.sel.healed,
                    shore_vals_start)
scale2 <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.sel.healed,
                    shore_vals_start, healed=FALSE) 

# For Model 3: ssf.map.mov.healed
shape3_T <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.mov.healed,
                      shore_vals_start)
scale3_T <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.mov.healed,
                      shore_vals_start, healed=TRUE) 

shape3_F <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.mov.healed,
                      shore_vals_start)
scale3_F <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.mov.healed,
                      shore_vals_start, healed=FALSE) 


# For Model 4: ssf.map.movsel.healed
shape4_T <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.mov.sel.healed,
                      shore_vals_start)
scale4_T <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.mov.sel.healed,
                      shore_vals_start, healed=TRUE) 

shape4_F <- shape.ssf(b1_shape, ssf.mov.sel.healed,
                     shore_vals_start)
scale4_F <- scale.ssf(b2_scale, ssf.mov.sel.healed,
                     shore_vals_start, healed=FALSE)

From it, we derive the matrix of step-length distribution for each model.

step_prob_matrix1 <- dgamma(step_length_matrix, 
                            shape = shape1, scale = scale1)
step_prob_matrix2 <- dgamma(step_length_matrix, 
                            shape = shape2, scale = scale2)
step_prob_matrix3_T <- dgamma(step_length_matrix, 
                              shape = shape3_T, scale = scale3_T)
step_prob_matrix3_F <- dgamma(step_length_matrix,
                              shape = shape3_F, scale = scale3_F)
step_prob_matrix4_T <- dgamma(step_length_matrix,
                              shape = shape4_T, scale = scale4_T)
step_prob_matrix4_F <- dgamma(step_length_matrix,
                              shape = shape4_F, scale = scale4_F)

We can now derive the movement kernel. Note that we do not incorporate turning angles, effectively ignoring directional correlation in the data. This simplification should introduce minimal bias because the effect of correlation becomes negligible when inferring long-term behaviour. As Hawkes (2009) observes “As sampling is carried out less frequently or after a large number of steps, CRW increasingly comes to resemble uncorrelated random walk (Okubo 1980). That is relevant in exploring the implications of the correlation identiﬁed in movement behaviour because CRW may generate distance distributions similar to or the same as those of uncorrelated random walk over time-scales relevant to dispersal”. In other words, over large scales and long time periods, the habitat use patterns of a correlated random walk are similar to those of an uncorrelated walk. Since the UD reflects the stationary equilibrium of habitat use patterns, neglecting the correlation in movement data when estimating it, should only introduce minimal bias.

Additionally, including turning angles would increase the dimensionality of the transition matrix, making it an n x n x M array, where \(M\) refers to the number of discrete bins used to represent the possible angles from \(0\) to \(2\pi\). This would make matrix inversion computationally infeasible, so ignoring turning angles is both theoretically reasonable and practically necessary.

movkernel_matrix <- step_prob_matrix1*
  exp(summary(ssf.noscars)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1]*shore_vals_end)
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix)
movkernel_matrix_norm1 <- t(t(movkernel_matrix)) / col_sums
#  Healed False
movkernel_matrix2_F <- step_prob_matrix2*
  exp((summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end))
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix2_F)
movkernel_matrix2_F_norm <- t(t(movkernel_matrix2_F) / col_sums)

#  Healed True
movkernel_matrix2_T <- step_prob_matrix2*
  exp((summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end) + 
        (summary(ssf.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end:Healed.Scars",1] * shore_vals_end))
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix2_T)
movkernel_matrix2_T_norm <- t(t(movkernel_matrix2_T) / col_sums)
#  Healed False
movkernel_matrix3_F <- step_prob_matrix3_F*
  exp(summary(ssf.mov.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end)
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix3_F)
movkernel_matrix3_F_norm <-  t(t(movkernel_matrix3_F) / col_sums)

#  Healed True
movkernel_matrix3_T <- step_prob_matrix3_T*
  exp(summary(ssf.mov.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end)
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix3_T)
movkernel_matrix3_T_norm <- t(t(movkernel_matrix3_T) / col_sums)
#  Healed False
movkernel_matrix4_F <- step_prob_matrix4_F*
  exp(summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end)
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix4_F)
movkernel_matrix4_F_norm <- t(t(movkernel_matrix4_F) / col_sums)

#  Healed True
movkernel_matrix4_T <- step_prob_matrix4_T*
  exp((summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end",1] * shore_vals_end) + 
        (summary(ssf.mov.sel.healed)$coef$cond["distShore.end:Healed.Scars",1] * shore_vals_end))
col_sums <- colSums(movkernel_matrix4_T)
movkernel_matrix4_T_norm <-  t(t(movkernel_matrix4_T) / col_sums)
get_eigenraster <- function(movkernel_matrix){
# Compute the eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue closest to 1
res <- eigs(movkernel_matrix, k = 1, sigma = 1)

eigenvalue <- res$values
eigenvector <- res$vectors 
eigenvector <- eigenvector / sum(eigenvector)
eigen_raster1 <- rast.grid


values(eigen_raster1) <- NA

# Assign eigenvector values to the water cells
eigen_raster1[water_cells] <- Re(eigenvector) 

# Normalize again
values(eigen_raster1)[water_cells] <- values(eigen_raster1)[water_cells] / 
                                     sum(values(eigen_raster1)[water_cells], na.rm = TRUE)
return(eigen_raster1)
}
eigen_raster1 <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix_norm1)
eigen_raster2_F <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix2_F_norm)
eigen_raster2_T <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix2_T_norm)
eigen_raster3_F <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix3_F_norm)
eigen_raster3_T <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix3_T_norm)
eigen_raster4_F <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix4_F_norm)
eigen_raster4_T <- get_eigenraster(movkernel_matrix4_T_norm)
ud.rasters <- list(
  noscars = eigen_raster1,
  sel.healed.F = eigen_raster2_F,
  sel.healed.T = eigen_raster2_T,
  mov.healed.F = eigen_raster3_F,
  mov.healed.T = eigen_raster3_T,
  sel.mov.healed.T = eigen_raster4_T,
  sel.mov.healed.F = eigen_raster4_F
)

Function to map UDs.

val.range.UD <- range(as.data.frame(ud.rasters))
mapping.UD <- function(model.name, col.box, plot.mar.l.UD = c(0.045, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)){
  map <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = ud.rasters[[model.name]]) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low=ssf.min.col, mid=ssf.mid.col, high=ssf.max.col,
                      midpoint = mean(val.range.UD), limit = val.range.UD, na.value = NA) +
    geom_sf(data=land, fill=land.col) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(st_bbox(ud.rasters[[model.name]])[1], st_bbox(ud.rasters[[model.name]])[3]),
           ylim = c(st_bbox(ud.rasters[[model.name]])[2], st_bbox(ud.rasters[[model.name]])[4]), expand = FALSE) +
    theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = col.box, fill=NA, linewidth = 0.5),
          legend.title = element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
          legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          legend.position = "top",
          axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(70, 80, by =1)) + 
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-90, -80, by = 5)) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title = "UD", order = 4,
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top"))) +
    theme(plot.margin = unit(plot.mar.l.UD, 'lines'))
  return(map)
}

Function to map the difference between the UDs of narwhals with and without scars.

mapping.UD.diff <- function(raster.dif,
                            col.box = "black", 
                            plot.mar.l.UD = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)){
  map <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = raster.dif) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = ssf.min.col, 
                         mid = ssf.mid.col, 
                         high = ssf.max.col, na.value = NA) +
    geom_sf(data=land, fill=land.col) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(st_bbox(raster.dif)[1], st_bbox(raster.dif)[3]),
           ylim = c(st_bbox(raster.dif)[2], st_bbox(raster.dif)[4]), expand = FALSE) +
    theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = col.box, fill=NA, linewidth = 0.5),
          axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
          axis.ticks = element_line(colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(70, 80, by =1)) + 
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-90, -80, by = 5)) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title = "Diff. in UD", 
                                 order = 4,
                                 theme = theme(legend.title = 
                                                 element_text(size = rel(legend.text.size)),
                                               legend.position = "top"))) +
    theme(plot.margin = unit(plot.mar.l.UD, 'lines'))
  return(map)
}
